key_points: Test at expected production rate to check loader adequacy and stockpile management
Mixing times are set and approved from plant uniformity testing results
sections.applicability: Applies to confirming batch plant capacity and mixing-time settings before production paving.

sections.title: Concrete Uniformity
sections.summary: Mixing difficulties (non-uniform discharge, excessive slump loss at the design w/cm) may indicate improper material sequencing, oversized batches, inadequate mixing time, admixture incompatibility, or temperature/moisture sensitivity, prompting plant/process/mixture-design changes or more uniformity testing.
sections.body: If difficulties in mixing or concrete uniformity are encountered, changes to the plant, changes in the mixing process, changes to the concrete mixture designs, or additional plant uniformity testing should be considered. Difficulties in concrete mixing at the design w/cm ratio, non-uniform concrete between the front and rear of the drum during discharge, and excessive loss in slump may indicate possible problems: materials not sequenced properly into the drum; too large a batch size relative to drum capacity; inadequate mixing times; liquid admixture incompatibility with cement or supplementary cementitious materials; sensitivity to initial concrete temperature; or sensitivity to stockpile moisture changes.
key_points: Symptoms: non-uniform front-to-rear drum discharge, excessive slump loss at the design w/cm ratio
Possible causes: material sequencing, batch size vs. drum capacity, mixing time, admixture incompatibility, temperature/moisture sensitivity
Response: adjust plant, mixing process, mixture design, or run additional uniformity testing
sections.applicability: Applies when diagnosing non-uniform or inconsistent concrete coming out of the batch plant.

sections.title: Concrete Delivery
sections.summary: Before production paving, verify batch-to-placement time limits, hauler adequacy against paver demand, and that delivered batch quantities match the approved mixture design, using the same delivery equipment as production.
sections.body: Evaluate the following concrete delivery processes before starting paving operations: check the time between water addition and depositing concrete on grade to verify batching/transport/dumping stays within specified time limits; add haulers if the paver stops and waits for concrete delivery; compare concrete material batch quantities with the approved mixture design; and deliver concrete using the same equipment as used in production (agitator trucks, open-end dump trucks, and other material-handling vehicles/equipment).
key_points: Verify the water-to-placement time stays within specified limits
Add haulers if the paver has to stop and wait for concrete
Compare actual batch quantities against the approved mixture design
Use the same delivery equipment in the test section as in production
sections.applicability: Applies to verifying concrete delivery logistics and timing ahead of production paving.

sections.title: Concrete Placement
sections.summary: Evaluate drop height (<=1.5 m/5 ft), segregation in dumped/spread concrete (triggering coarse-aggregate uniformity testing if suspected), truck-to-truck aggregate-content consistency, and dowel-basket alignment/installation during slipforming.
sections.body: Evaluate the following concrete placement operations before starting paving operations: concrete dumped from trucks, chuted from agitator trucks, or spread using belt spreaders should not drop more than 1.5 m (5 ft); concrete dumped on grade or placed in front of the paver using belt placers or spreaders must be examined for aggregate segregation, and if it appears segregated, uniformity testing on coarse aggregate content must be conducted; significant differences in aggregate content between samples from the same truck indicate that transport or dumping processes may need to be modified; and when concrete is dumped in front of the paver or spreader and dowel baskets are placed during slipforming, observe the alignment procedures to ensure baskets are properly located and installed.
key_points: Concrete drop height limit: 1.5 m (5 ft)
Examine dumped/spread concrete for segregation; conduct coarse-aggregate uniformity testing if segregation is suspected
Truck-to-truck aggregate content differences indicate a transport/dumping process problem
Observe dowel-basket alignment procedures when baskets are placed during slipforming
sections.applicability: Applies to evaluating placement technique, including dowel basket handling, during test section paving.

sections.title: Quality Assurance/Quality Control
sections.summary: Before production paving, evaluate sampling/testing of slump/air/temperature/unit weight, sample transport and central-location curing procedures, and fabricate beams/cylinders more frequently than sublot limits to better characterize batch-to-batch variability.
sections.body: Evaluate the following concrete sampling and QA/QC operations before starting paving operations, addressing deficiencies concerning acceptance, QA and QC, concrete sampling, transporting, beam fabrication, initial and final curing procedures, testing, and corrective action: sample concrete in front of the paver and test for slump, air content, initial concrete temperature, and plastic unit weight per project requirements, checking concrete air content behind the paver and documenting ambient air temperatures; properly transport concrete samples for beam or cylinder fabrication if fabricated and initially cured at a central location, fabricating extra samples for testing at different ages (early-age tests verify strength gain relative to the mixture design and establish relative opening times); and fabricate beams and cylinders at intervals more frequent than the sublot limits to better indicate variability from minor changes in batch quantities throughout the day.
key_points: Sample and test slump, air content, initial temperature, and plastic unit weight in front of the paver; check air behind the paver too
Fabricate extra beam/cylinder samples at different ages to verify early-age strength gain and opening times
Fabricate beams/cylinders more frequently than sublot limits during the test section to better characterize variability
sections.applicability: Applies to QA/QC sampling and testing procedures exercised during test section construction.

sections.title: Consolidation and Finishing
sections.summary: Diagnose consolidation/finishing problems (smoothness, edge slump, surface closure/tearing) via vibrator adjustment, slump-loss/incompatibility checks, thickness verification, blockout/embedded-steel monitoring, and controlled water/finishing effort to avoid laitance.
sections.body: Evaluate the following before starting paving operations: difficulties in placing, consolidation, maintaining a smooth pavement and tolerable edge slump, closing the surface/edges, and surface tearing indicate problems with the concrete, mixture design, or paver operation; adjust vibrator frequency, spacing, and elevation if consolidation problems occur, and add supplementary vibrators at longitudinal construction joints if entrapped air/honeycombing appears along vertical edges; if consolidation problems are attributed to the concrete, conduct plant slump-loss tests (an incompatibility problem is suspected if slump loss exceeds 25 mm [1 in.]) and verify aggregate moisture monitoring; dowel bar inserters are prohibited on DoD airfield projects; verify pavement thickness by probing or piano wire/ruler methods; transfer transverse joint stations from the base/forms to the pavement surface for sawcutting reference; observe blockouts for movement and check embedded steel behind the paver for security/disturbance; examine the surface behind the screed/tube float for tearing (linked to slump loss/excess, poor adjustment, or excess speed) and for closure (premature stiffening, insufficient paste, vibrator frequency/elevation, paving speed, or grout box mortar); measure edge slump frequently, adjustable via aggregate content, water content, mortar content, paver side-form batter, or reduced speed; and examine the surface with a straight edge after finishing but before texturing, avoiding added water (a fine mist only, if needed) since excess laitance indicates over-finishing or excess water.
key_points: Adjust vibrator frequency/spacing/elevation for consolidation problems; add supplementary vibrators at longitudinal joints if needed
Slump loss > 25 mm (1 in.) at the plant suggests a material incompatibility problem
Dowel bar inserters are prohibited on DoD airfield projects
Measure edge slump frequently; adjustable via aggregate/water/mortar content, paver batter, or speed
Avoid adding water during finishing; excess laitance signals over-finishing or excess water
sections.applicability: Applies to diagnosing and correcting consolidation and finishing issues observed during test section paving.

sections.title: Texturing
sections.summary: Inspect texturing for appearance uniformity; if burlap drag is used it must be wet enough to roughen the surface without exposing/rolling coarse aggregate, and ponded laitance/thick water films indicate excessively wet burlap.
sections.body: The method of texturing must be inspected for uniformity in appearance. If burlap is used, it must be wet enough to provide a rough surface texture without exposing or rolling any coarse aggregates; ponding of laitance or the depositing of thick films of water is indicative of the burlap being excessively wet.
key_points: Inspect texturing method for uniform appearance
Burlap drag: wet enough to roughen texture without exposing/rolling coarse aggregate
Ponded laitance or thick water films indicate the burlap is too wet
sections.applicability: Applies to evaluating texturing operations during test section (and production) paving.

sections.title: Curing
sections.summary: Establish curing compound coverage rates before test strip construction (dependent on the applied texture), apply uniformly along the surface and vertical edges, and recognize non-uniform coverage as a sign of nozzle/speed/mixing/pass-count problems.
sections.body: Consider the following concrete curing operations before starting paving operations: establish curing compound coverage rates prior to test strip construction, since coverage rate depends on the surface texture applied; apply curing compound uniformly along the pavement surface and vertical edges; and recognize non-uniform application as indicative of spray nozzles set too low, clogged nozzles, cure rig speed set too fast, insufficient mixing of curing compound, or an insufficient number of passes.
key_points: Set curing compound coverage rates before test strip construction (texture-dependent)
Apply uniformly along the surface AND the vertical edges
Non-uniform coverage signals nozzle height/clogging, rig speed, mixing, or pass-count problems
sections.applicability: Applies to evaluating curing compound application during test section paving.

sections.title: Sawcutting
sections.summary: Monitor fresh-concrete temperature (every ~20 min) or maturity via inward-placed thermocouples to establish sawcutting time; allow trial cuts slightly early, then repeat cutting/visual rating until owner, contractor, and inspector agree the sawcuts meet requirements.
sections.body: Consider the following concrete sawcutting operations before paving: periodically monitor the temperature of fresh concrete if maturity meters, infrared guns, or surface thermometers are used to establish sawcutting times, sampling approximately every 20 minutes until joints are ready; if using the maturity meter technique, insert thermocouples into the plastic concrete as soon as possible after texturing, positioned at least 0.6 m (2 ft) inward from pavement edges for representative temperatures; allow sawcut operators to initiate cutting when concrete is slightly too green to calibrate temperature/maturity measurements; cut several meters (feet) to allow a visual rating or quantify joint raveling, repeating until representatives for owner, contractor, and inspector agree sawcuts meet project requirements; document conditions of sawcuts and photograph to avoid future disputes, documenting the maturity/temperature at which 'acceptable' sawcuts can be made for production paving; and check sawcut depths for each saw used, carrying transverse sawcuts through the longitudinal free edges or as close to forms as possible.
key_points: Monitor temperature ~every 20 minutes, or use maturity meters with thermocouples placed >=0.6 m (2 ft) from pavement edges
Deliberately allow trial cuts slightly too early to calibrate the temperature/maturity threshold
Repeat cutting/rating until owner, contractor, and inspector all agree sawcuts meet requirements
Document and photograph sawcut conditions and the maturity/temperature basis for 'acceptable' production sawcutting
sections.applicability: Applies to establishing and calibrating sawcutting timing during test section construction.

sections.title: Test Section Acceptance
sections.summary: After test strip construction, a final inspection covers surface/edge condition, texture/curing coverage, headers/sawcut joints, blockout areas, edge slump/profile, and cores for thickness/consolidation/segregation.
sections.body: After test strip construction, perform a final inspection of the pavement, covering: condition of the surface and slipformed edges; texture and curing compound coverage; headers and sawcut joints; blockout areas (light can penetrations or other utilities); edge slump and profile (straight edge or profile testing); and cores (for thickness and assessing consolidation and segregation). See ASTM D6938 for in-place density/water content testing by nuclear methods.
key_points: Final inspection covers surface/edge condition, texture, curing coverage, headers, sawcut joints, blockouts
Includes edge slump/profile testing and cores for thickness/consolidation/segregation
ASTM D6938 governs in-place density/water content testing by nuclear methods
sections.applicability: Applies to the final go/no-go inspection of a completed test section before production paving proceeds.

sections.title: Adjustments to Quality Control/Quality Assurance Operations
sections.summary: Document/discuss deficiencies found during or after test section construction, hold owner-contractor meetings to agree on corrective actions, and consider CQC plan/operation changes before production pavement construction begins.
sections.body: Document and discuss any deficiencies noted during test section construction or post-construction inspection and testing techniques. Hold meetings between the contracting officer and the contractor to review the test section results, and agree on actions to address and resolve deficiencies before commencing production pavement construction. Consider making any necessary changes in the CQC plan and operations.
key_points: Document and discuss all deficiencies from test section construction and post-construction inspection
Contracting officer and contractor meet to agree on corrective actions before production paving
Update the CQC plan/operations as needed based on test section results
sections.applicability: Applies to closing out the test section process and carrying lessons learned into production paving.
